messages:
incidents-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: increased container restarts detected in cluster-prod (node-pool: gpu-prefill-3). metric: container_restart_count spiked from 0.2/min to 6/min in last 3m. possible cause: prefill OOMs for long context requests. auto-pager sent to oncall.

ravi: taking pager. looking now — any customer reports?

jamie: seeing spikes for model:redwood-large-ctx on pool gpu-prefill-3. A bunch of requests with prefill token counts > 150k. stack: container restarted w/ SIGKILL.

sarah: logs from one container: ```
I0524 21:03:12.123456 PrefillAllocator.cpp:172] allocating 28.4G for kv-cache
terminate called after throwing an instance of 'std::bad_alloc'
Aborted (core dumped)
```

alex: that's classic GPU OOM during prefill. Are we seeing driver resets / CUDA errors?

jamie: yes, earlier entries: ```
E0524 21:02:59.987654 cudart: cuCtxCreate() failed: out of memory (2)
E0524 21:03:00.000012 container_manager: restarting container
```

ravi: immediate mitigation suggestions: 1) divert new traffic for that model off gpu-prefill-3 to other pools; 2) enable fallback to quantized-smaller for long-context requests; 3) temporarily cap PREFILL_MAX_TOKENS for that route to 32k. I'm going to cordon the node pool to avoid new pods scheduling while we triage.

jamie: running command to cordon nodes in the pool: `kubectl get nodes -l pool=gpu-prefill-3 -o name | xargs -n1 kubectl cordon` — in progress.

oncall-bot: Pager rotation: ravi oncall until 22:00 UTC. Please post handoff if you leave.

sarah: I pushed a policy tweak to the routing layer to divert 40% of new traffic for model:redwood-large-ctx to gpu-prefill-1 and gpu-prefill-2, prioritizing warm KV caches, canary only. Watching.

alex: can we set a runtime env to enforce a prefill token cap per-request for the model? if so, do it as a hotpatch.

ravi: applying hotpatch: `kubectl set env deployment/redwood-serving PREFILL_TOKEN_CAP=32000 --namespace=prod` — applied to the canary subset. Rolling out to remaining replicas after 5m of stability.

jamie: after diversion and cap, restart rate dropped to 0.9/min on that pool. latency for some requests rose ~120ms due to rerouting. Customer-facing error rate (502/503) down from 8% to 1.5% for the affected model.

sarah: found an example request body that triggered 180k prefill tokens — likely a bug in customer prompt generation (looping). reached out to AE to notify customer id: cust-8421, request samples attached.

alex: long-term: we should add server-side hard cap enforcement + prefill accounting metrics exposed to routes (prefill_tokens per request) and an evaluation to drop/trim extremely large prefill before scheduling GPU allocation. Filing a follow-up ticket.

ravi: agree. For now, I'm going to drain the worst nodes and trigger a rolling restart for the affected daemonset to clear fragmentation. Command: `kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` — doing one at a time.

jamie: FYI - noticed on one node a lot of smaller containers accumulating GPU memory fragmentation even after restart; kernel-level CUDA driver shows high vram allocation fragmentation. Might need driver restart on those hosts if drains don't help.

oncall-bot: incident severity updated to sev2 (SLA impact: partial). Notifying SRE lead.

ravi: handover notes for next oncall (in ~20m): keep diversion in place until prefills < 32k for 30m and container restart rate < 0.5/min. If restarts persist, escalate to infra for driver restart and consider temporarily scaling capacity.

sarah: AE confirmed they've contacted customer and applied a temporary client-side rate limit / prompt validation. They expect fix within 4 hours.

alex: created follow-up GH: infra/serving#478 - "enforce server-side prefill token cap + prefilter extreme prefill" with rollout plan and metrics.

ravi: marking incident as mitigated for immediate customer impact. Leaving monitoring alerts at higher sensitivity for 3h. Passing to next oncall: sarah taking overnight watch. please call if anything spikes. :thumbsup:

sarah: taking watch. I'll post a summary and timeline in #incidents-summary and update the postmortem template once we collect logs.

incidents-bot: Incident closed for now (mitigated): root cause: GPU OOM during prefill caused by extreme long-context requests. Actions: traffic diversion, PREFILL_TOKEN_CAP hotpatch, node drains. Next steps: postmortem, server-side safeguards, AE customer fix.
